newsitem.title: FRANCE: British war graves among 80 desecrated in France.
newsitem.headline: British war graves among 80 desecrated in France.

text.p: Unknown attackers desecrated about 80 graves, including those of five British soldiers killed in World War One, in a northern French cemetery overnight, police said on Sunday.

Wooden and marble crosses were uprooted and broken, commemorative plaques smashed and flowerpots overturned in the attacks in the Merville cemetery close to the Belgian border, the latest in a series of graveyard attacks in the region.
"The investigation is under way, we don't have any leads for the time being," said gendarmerie Captain Jacques Bance in the nearby town of Hazebrouck.

He said there was apparently no pattern to the desecration in the Merville village cemetery, where British soldiers who fought German troops are buried alongside local citizens. Five British graves were damaged along with about 75 French.
In July, almost 200 graves, mostly of British soldiers from the 1914-18 war, were desecrated in military cemeteries in the region. France's centre-right government strongly condemned the attacks.
